gemini.depth_why: The scenery is accessible only during the brief Antarctic summer, with the rest of the year closed to visitors.
gemini.overview: The Antarctic Peninsula is defined by its ice and coastal scenery, seen almost entirely from ships and Zodiacs. Glaciers calve directly into the ocean, and massive icebergs drift through narrow passages like the Lemaire Channel. The landscape is stark, consisting of steep, snow-covered mountains rising straight from the water.

blurbs.text: The days are very long, and open water lets ships and Zodiacs weave between icebergs, with the Lemaire Channel often passable.
Sea ice can still block narrow channels and bays, so some landings and the Lemaire Channel may be out of reach, but the snow on the shores and mountains is pristine.
The days are shorter, the snow cover is thinner and more rock shows along the shores.
Thick sea ice and storms close the peninsula, and no passenger ships sail.

gemini.overview: Chicago's scenery is defined by its vast lakefront and the river that cuts through downtown. The primary views are of the city skyline rising directly from the shores of Lake Michigan, best seen from the water or the lakefront trail.

blurbs.text: Boat tours run frequently on the river and lake, providing the main vantage points for the skyline.
Boat tours reduce their schedules as the lakefront cools.
Ice often forms on Lake Michigan, and the bitter winds keep most people away from the open waterfront.
Boat tours begin to resume their routes on the river and lake.

gemini.depth_why: The experience of the lakefront and river views changes with the weather and the operating seasons of the boat tours.
Scores vary significantly by season due to snow cover, trail access, and mountain pass closures.
gemini.overview: The Dolomites are famed for sheer, pale limestone peaks rising abruptly from green alpine meadows. Signature views include the three jagged pillars of Tre Cime di Lavaredo and the vast, rolling high plateau of Alpe di Siusi. Deep valleys hold forests and lakes, most notably the emerald waters of Lago di Braies beneath steep rock walls.

blurbs.text: Snow covers the meadows and high passes, turning the region into a winter landscape. Many high-elevation hiking trails and scenic drives are closed or require winter gear, but the snow-capped peaks offer a different kind of scenery from the valley floors and ski areas.
Melting snow and mud cover the valleys, and the summer lifts and mountain huts are still closed, so the signature viewpoints are hard to reach.
The big Val Gardena lifts to Seceda and Alpe di Siusi open around the third week of the month and the Tre Cime toll road in late May, weather permitting, but snow often lingers on the highest trails.

The high passes and trails are fully open and the lifts run, giving clear access to the iconic viewpoints (Seceda's lifts and the Tre Cime toll road both need advance booking). The pale rock against the bright green of Alpe di Siusi is at its sharpest, and Lago di Braies is fully thawed.

Golden larch forests add a new layer to the scenery. Lifts and huts close one by one, the Tre Cime toll road shuts as soon as snow or ice threatens, and even the main Val Gardena lifts stop running within days of the month's end. Early snow can close higher trails.
The summer lifts, mountain huts and the Tre Cime toll road are closed, and snow begins to close the high passes and trails, while the valleys are bare and cold before the ski lifts open.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise from winter lows to a summer peak when ferries run and the caldera views are clearest.
gemini.overview: Santorini and the Cyclades are known for their dramatic coastal scenery and whitewashed villages built into steep cliffs. The signature view is the Santorini caldera, a flooded volcanic crater best seen from the towns of Oia and Fira. Beyond the famous sunsets, the islands offer rugged coastlines, volcanic beaches, and boat trips to the central volcano.

blurbs.text: Winter brings the wet season, with frequent rain and wind that can obscure the caldera views. Many ferries and boat tours to the volcano stop running, limiting access to the coastal scenery.
Spring weather brings clearer skies and better visibility of the cliffs and villages, and fuller ferry schedules make it easier to reach the viewpoints and volcanic beaches.
Clear skies give the best views of the famous Oia and Fira sunsets over the caldera. Boat trips to the volcano run frequently, and the coastal scenery is easy to reach.
October still provides good visibility for the caldera and coastal views, though the chance of rain increases late in the month. Most boat tours and ferries continue to operate.

gemini.depth_why: Scores drop in the wet winter months when visibility and access can be affected by rain and high water.
gemini.overview: Venice's scenery is defined by its canals, lagoons, and historic architecture. The signature views are the Grand Canal and St. Mark's Square, where the water meets the city. Beyond the main islands, the Venetian Lagoon offers views of marshlands and smaller islands like Murano and Burano. The best time to see the city and lagoon is during the drier months from spring through autumn.

blurbs.text: High water (acqua alta) often floods low-lying areas such as St. Mark's Square, and fog is common, reducing visibility across the lagoon and along the canals.

Drier weather and clearer skies make this the best time to view the Grand Canal and explore the wider Venetian Lagoon. The light is better for seeing the contrast between the water and the city's architecture.

gemini.depth_why: Scores vary based on the visibility of the Milky Way core and changes in night cloud cover.
gemini.overview: The Canary Islands offer some of the darkest and clearest skies in the world, thanks to high-altitude volcanic peaks that sit above the clouds. Visitors can drive up to viewpoints in Teide National Park on Tenerife or Roque de los Muchachos on La Palma for very dark skies. The best conditions align with the months when the Milky Way's bright core is visible.

blurbs.text: The Milky Way's bright core is visible in the night sky, a great time to look up from the high volcanic slopes. Spring brings slightly more cloud cover at night, but the high-altitude viewpoints often stay clear.

The Milky Way's core is well placed for viewing through the evening and night. The nights are shorter in summer, and night clouds are more frequent, but the high peaks usually remain above the cloud layer.
The Milky Way's bright core is still visible, and the nights grow longer. Night cloud cover drops, providing some of the clearest and darkest skies of the year for stargazing from the national parks.
The Milky Way's core is below the horizon, but the long nights offer plenty of time to view the winter constellations. The skies remain very dark, and night cloud cover is relatively low.

gemini.depth_why: The sky never gets fully dark from April to August, while the rest of the year offers varying hours of darkness and cloud cover.
gemini.overview: Finnish Lapland offers very dark skies away from the towns, making it a strong destination for stargazing during the colder months. The region's high latitude means the sky never gets fully dark from spring through late summer, but the long nights of autumn and winter provide ample time to look up. While cloud cover is frequent, clear nights reveal a sky dark enough to see the Milky Way and countless stars.

blurbs.text: The nights are very long. Cloud cover is heavy, but when there is a gap in the cloud, the stargazing is excellent. The Milky Way's bright core is not visible.
March brings the best balance of darkness and clearer skies. The nights are still long, and the cloud begins to thin out compared with deep winter.
The sun stays too close to the horizon and the sky never gets fully dark, so only the brightest stars and planets show, if any.
The sky gets properly dark again on clear nights, though clouds are common. The Milky Way's bright core is visible before it dips below the horizon for the winter.
The nights lengthen quickly. Heavy cloud cover is the main challenge, often hiding the stars, but clear nights give very dark skies.

gemini.depth_why: The stargazing experience changes with the wet and dry seasons, affecting cloud cover and the position of the Milky Way.
gemini.overview: Namibia has some of the darkest and clearest night skies available to travelers, anchored by the certified dark-sky reserve at NamibRand Nature Reserve. The vast, dry desert landscapes and minimal light pollution make it an exceptional destination for observing the stars and the Milky Way. The best viewing aligns with the dry months from May to October when the skies are mostly clear and the nights are long.

blurbs.text: The wet season brings frequent night clouds, significantly reducing visibility.
Cloud cover begins to decrease, offering more clear nights for stargazing.
The skies clear up significantly following the wet season, and the nights grow longer, providing excellent dark skies.
Skies are mostly clear and the nights long, creating ideal conditions. The bright core of the Milky Way is well placed for viewing across the desert.
The skies remain very clear, though the nights gradually shorten. The Milky Way core is no longer at its best, but the stars are highly visible.
Cloud cover increases as the wet season approaches, and the nights are shorter. The sky is still very dark when clear.

gemini.depth_why: The wet season brings heavier cloud cover, while the rest of the year is slightly clearer but still washed out.
gemini.overview: Singapore's night sky is heavily washed out by city lights, making stargazing very difficult. Only the brightest stars and planets are visible through the urban glow. Cloud is frequent and limits visibility further.

blurbs.text: The skies are slightly drier, which gives the best chance to spot the brightest stars, though heavy light pollution and frequent clouds keep the sky washed out.
The wet season brings heavy cloud cover almost every night, leaving very few chances to see any stars through the city glow.

gemini.depth_why: Scores change based on the wet and dry seasons and the visibility of the Milky Way core.
gemini.overview: Salar de Uyuni offers some of the darkest skies on Earth, with a vast, flat expanse that makes the horizon feel endless. The high altitude and extremely dry air create exceptionally clear conditions for viewing the stars and the Milky Way. The best viewing aligns with the dry season when night clouds are rare.

blurbs.text: The wet season brings frequent night clouds, which often block the stars. When the sky does clear, the darkness is profound, though the bright core of the Milky Way is not visible at night.
Cloud cover begins to decrease as the wet season ends. The skies are very dark, offering good stargazing during clear breaks.
The dry season begins, bringing mostly clear skies and excellent visibility. The bright core of the Milky Way starts to become visible late in the night.
The dry season brings mostly clear skies and long nights of astronomical darkness. The bright core of the Milky Way is well placed for viewing, though nights on the salt flats are very cold.
The skies remain very dark and mostly clear. The Milky Way core is still visible early in the night before setting.
Cloud cover begins to increase as the dry season ends, but the skies remain very dark when clear.

gemini.depth_why: Scores form distinct groups based on the transition from the hot, dry summer to the cooler wet season.
gemini.overview: The Algarve is known for its long sandy beaches and extensive resort pools. Visitors can lie out at beach clubs along the coast or relax by the water at inland retreats. The dry summer months offer the most reliable heat and sunshine.

blurbs.text: The wet season brings cooler weather and more rain, leaving the beaches and resort pools mostly empty.
Temperatures remain below 70 degrees, keeping most visitors away from the loungers despite increasing sunshine.
Warm days return with highs in the mid-70s, offering fair conditions for a few hours in the sun before the summer heat arrives.
The dry summer brings hot, sunny days ideal for lying out at beach clubs or resort pools.
Afternoon highs drop into the mid-70s, though sunny days still occur.

gemini.depth_why: Aruba's weather is consistently warm and sunny year-round, with only minor variations in rain and heat, so one blurb covers the whole year.
gemini.overview: Aruba is known for its reliable sunshine and warm weather. Visitors can choose between expansive resort pools and white-sand beaches lined with loungers and beach clubs. The island's arid climate means there is no true wet season, making it a dependable choice for sunshine any time of year.

blurbs.text: Warm temperatures and abundant sunshine are the norm. The island's resort pools and beach clubs offer plenty of spots to relax, with trade winds providing a breeze on the hottest afternoons.
Rain is at its most frequent and cloud cover increases, though showers are usually brief and temperatures stay warm.

gemini.depth_why: The year is divided into a short, warm summer peak, marginal shoulder months, and a long, cold off-season.
gemini.overview: Cape Cod and the Islands offer miles of sandy coastline, from the calm shores of Cape Cod Bay to the expansive beaches of Nantucket and Martha's Vineyard. Visitors can relax on quiet dunes or find a spot near the water, though beach clubs with loungers are rare. The season is short, peaking in the hot months of July and August when afternoon temperatures reach the upper 70s.

blurbs.text: Cold; highs stay in the 30s and 40s.
Highs only reach the 50s and low 60s, though the days are lengthening.
June warms up to the low 70s. The beaches are sunny, but the air can still feel brisk.
Afternoon highs are in the upper 70s and the days are long and sunny. This is the prime time to lay a towel on the sand at places like the Cape Cod National Seashore.
September still sees highs in the low 70s, offering a few warm afternoons on the quieter beaches, though the sun sets earlier.
Temperatures drop into the 60s and 50s. It is generally too chilly to lie out on the sand, though a rare warm afternoon might allow a brief sit in the sun.

gemini.depth_why: Scores are very low year-round, divided into a slightly brighter summer and a dark, cold winter.
gemini.overview: Iceland's cool climate and frequent winds keep temperatures well below typical beach weather even in midsummer. Visitors who want to relax outdoors head to the country's geothermally heated pools. The warmest and brightest days happen in midsummer, though afternoon highs rarely reach 60 degrees.

blurbs.text: Daylight is long and the weather is the year's warmest, but afternoon highs remain in the 50s. Catching a few rays mostly means finding a spot sheltered from the wind.
Short days, frequent rain, and temperatures in the 30s and 40s make lying out in the sun impractical.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise and fall with the temperature, creating distinct seasons for pool days.
gemini.overview: Sedona has numerous resort pools, set against the backdrop of the red rocks. Visitors can also find natural spots to lie out along the shores of Oak Creek. The warm, sunny climate makes it a reliable destination for lounging by the water from late spring through early fall.

blurbs.text: Winter highs in the 50s and low 60s mean the air is too cold to lie out comfortably.
As spring begins, highs approach 70 degrees. The warmest afternoons might allow for some pool time in the sun.
Highs reach the mid-70s and sunny days are frequent. It is a pleasant time to relax by a resort pool, though the air can still feel crisp.
Resort pool days are ideal, with afternoon highs often reaching into the 90s. The sun is intense, making the water a welcome relief.
Temperatures cool into the upper 70s, offering comfortable, sunny afternoons for lounging by a heated pool or along Oak Creek.
Afternoon highs drop into the 60s, making it too chilly for most to lie out, though sheltered resort pools may still offer a brief window in the midday sun.

gemini.depth_why: Scores are high across the board, but the cold months get a slight bump for the contrast of freezing air and hot outdoor thermal pools.
gemini.overview: The Black Forest is a historic center for thermal bathing, anchored by famous spa towns like Baden-Baden and Bad Wildbad. Visitors soak in mineral-rich hot springs, visit grand 19th-century bathhouses, and stay at dedicated wellness resorts tucked into the wooded hills. Be aware that German saunas are usually nude and often mixed-gender.

blurbs.text: Freezing air contrasts with the hot outdoor mineral pools, the traditional peak for thermal bathing.
The warmer weather makes outdoor soaking less dramatic, but the grand bathhouses and clinical wellness retreats operate fully.

gemini.depth_why: Scores peak in the snowy winter months for outdoor bathing and dip slightly in the warmer summer.
gemini.overview: Hokkaido is a major destination for traditional Japanese bathing, driven by its geothermal activity and historic onsen towns. Visitors come for the thermal bath culture, which ranges from rustic outdoor pools (rotenburo) to large resort complexes in districts like Noboribetsu and Jozankei. Bathing here is typically nude and gender-segregated, and many facilities prohibit visible tattoos.

blurbs.text: Soaking in an outdoor rotenburo surrounded by deep snow is a classic Hokkaido experience, with a sharp contrast between the freezing air and the steaming thermal water.

Spring brings milder weather to the spa towns. The melting snow reveals the rocky landscapes around the outdoor baths, making it a comfortable time to hop between different thermal pools in resort areas without the intense winter chill.

The outdoor baths are surrounded by lush green foliage. The hot water is less of a contrast to the air temperature, but the long daylight hours allow for extended evening soaks in the forested valleys.

Autumn transforms the scenery around the outdoor baths with bright fall foliage. The crisp, cooling air makes the hot thermal waters highly appealing again, drawing visitors to the mountain spa districts for seasonal retreats.

gemini.depth_why: Hammams are indoor bathhouses that operate without seasonal changes.
gemini.overview: Istanbul is a major center for traditional Turkish baths, known as hammams, which have been part of the city's culture for centuries. Visitors can experience authentic bathing rituals that include resting on heated marble slabs, vigorous scrubbing, and foam massages in historic, domed bathhouses. The city also features modern day spas and clinical wellness centers.

blurbs.text: Historic hammams offer the traditional sequence of a steam room, a scrub by an attendant, and a foam massage. Men and women bathe in separate sections or during segregated hours, and guests are typically provided with a peshtemal towel to wear.

gemini.depth_why: Scores are grouped into the traditional monsoon peak for Ayurveda and the rest of the year.
gemini.overview: Kerala is a premier global destination for Ayurveda, offering everything from luxury wellness resorts to intensive clinical treatments. Visitors come for traditional therapies like Shirodhara and Panchakarma, administered at dedicated Ayurvedic hospitals and retreats. The state's humid climate is considered ideal for these oil-based treatments.

blurbs.text: The wet monsoon is traditionally the most highly regarded time for Ayurvedic treatments. The high humidity is believed to open the body's pores, making it more receptive to herbal oils and intensive cure-style therapies.

Wellness resorts and day spas operate fully, offering a wide range of massages and wellness programs. The drier weather is comfortable for combining spa treatments with general travel, though traditionalists favor the monsoon for deep clinical cures.

gemini.depth_why: Jjimjilbangs and day spas are indoor facilities with no seasonal closures.
gemini.overview: Seoul is a major destination for Korean bathhouse culture, known as jjimjilbangs, alongside high-end day spas. Visitors can experience traditional kiln saunas, hot and cold soaking pools, and vigorous full-body scrubs. In jjimjilbangs, the wet bathing areas are nude and gender-segregated, while the dry saunas and lounging spaces are mixed-gender and require the provided cotton uniforms.

blurbs.text: Jjimjilbangs function as social hubs with heated floors, sleeping mats, and snack bars selling roasted eggs and sweet rice drink (sikhye). High-end day spas in districts like Gangnam provide advanced facials and traditional Korean herbal treatments.
